## Reaction-space Jacobian (`evolve_temperature`) {#sec-ch06-jacobian}

### Summary

An implicit step needs the derivative of every reaction rate with respect to every species concentration. kintera
returns it in reaction space, one row per reaction, so that the caller multiplies it by the stoichiometric matrix.
It combines the derivative of the mass-action product with the derivative of the rate constant that autograd
returned in @sec-ch06-mass-action, and, when temperature evolves, a term for the heating by reaction.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $J_{jk} = \partial r_j / \partial c_k$, @eq-ch06-jacobian-entry.

**Data.** $T$, $c$, volumetric heat capacity, rates, $\partial k/\partial c$, optional $\partial k/\partial T$ and rate constants.

**Placement.** After `forward_with_rate_constants`, before `evolve_implicit`.

**Activation.** Always called by the driver; the temperature term only with `evolve_temperature`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Needs explicit rate constants where a condensate is zero.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $J_{jk}$, entry of the reaction-space Jacobian [$\mathrm{s^{-1}}$]; $C_V$, volumetric heat capacity
[$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$]; $u_k$, molar internal energy of species $k$ [$\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$].

### Derivation

**At fixed temperature.** Write the rate of @eq-ch06-mass-action-rate as $r_j = k_j(T, c)\, P_j(c)$, with
$P_j = \prod_i c_i^{\nu_{ij}}$ the mass-action product. The rate constant may depend on the concentrations through a
third body (@sec-ch06-falloff) or a saturation deficit (@sec-ch06-evaporation). The product rule gives

$$
\left(\frac{\partial r_j}{\partial c_k}\right)_T = P_j\, \frac{\partial k_j}{\partial c_k} + k_j \frac{\partial P_j}{\partial c_k}
= P_j\, \frac{\partial k_j}{\partial c_k} + \nu_{kj}\, \frac{r_j}{c_k} ,
$$ {#eq-ch06-jacobian-entry}

because $\partial P_j / \partial c_k = \nu_{kj} P_j / c_k$. For an evaporation column the product is the condensate
concentration $c_p$ alone, so the second term is $k_j\, \partial c_p / \partial c_k$, which is $k_j$ for the
condensate and 0 for the gases. `jacobian` forms @eq-ch06-jacobian-entry
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::jacobian >}}).

**Temperature follows from energy.** With `evolve_temperature` the step is taken in a closed cell at fixed volume with
no heating from outside. The first law then holds the internal energy per volume fixed,

$$
U = \sum_k c_k\, u_k(T) \quad [\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}] ,
$$

with $u_k$ the molar internal energy of species $k$, including its reference offset (@sec-ch03-species-functions).
A change of the concentrations at fixed $U$ must therefore change the temperature:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 = \mathrm{d}U &= \sum_k u_k\, \mathrm{d}c_k + \Big(\sum_k c_k \frac{\mathrm{d}u_k}{\mathrm{d}T}\Big)\, \mathrm{d}T \\
&= \sum_k u_k\, \mathrm{d}c_k + C_V\, \mathrm{d}T ,
\end{aligned}
$$

where $C_V = \sum_k c_k\, c_{v,k}$ is the heat capacity at constant volume per unit volume
[$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$]. Solving for $\mathrm{d}T$,

$$
\left(\frac{\partial T}{\partial c_k}\right)_U = -\frac{u_k}{C_V} .
$$ {#eq-ch06-jacobian-dtdc}

Raising the concentration of a species with a large (positive) energy content at fixed $U$ cools the cell, because
that energy has to come from the thermal part. `jacobian`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::jacobian >}}) does not form @eq-ch06-jacobian-dtdc on its own: it
takes $u_k$ from `eval_intEng_R` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_intEng_R >}}), which returns $u_k/\mathcal R$,
and divides by the caller's $C_V$ inside the term below.

**Chain rule.** The rate depends on $c$ directly and through $T(c)$. At fixed $U$,

$$
\left(\frac{\partial r_j}{\partial c_k}\right)_U = \left(\frac{\partial r_j}{\partial c_k}\right)_T
+ \left(\frac{\partial r_j}{\partial T}\right)_c \left(\frac{\partial T}{\partial c_k}\right)_U
= \left(\frac{\partial r_j}{\partial c_k}\right)_T - P_j\, \frac{\partial k_j}{\partial T}\, \frac{u_k}{C_V} ,
$$ {#eq-ch06-jacobian-feedback}

since only the rate constant depends on $T$, so $(\partial r_j/\partial T)_c = P_j\, \partial k_j/\partial T$, and
$(\partial T/\partial c_k)_U$ is @eq-ch06-jacobian-dtdc.
@eq-ch06-jacobian-entry and @eq-ch06-jacobian-feedback are computed in `jacobian`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::jacobian >}}). It forms the first as `concp_fwd * rc_ddC +
mass_derivative`
and subtracts the second with $u_k = \mathcal R \cdot$ `eval_intEng_R` and $C_V$ the caller's argument `cvol`.
Two consistency conditions follow. The energies must be the same functions, offsets included, that the
thermodynamics uses to recover $T$ from $U$ (@sec-ch03-thermo-y); otherwise the linearisation targets a different
$T(U)$. And `cvol` must be the heat capacity at constant volume.

The check differentiates $r(c, T(c))$ by central differences, with $T$ solved from fixed $U$ at each perturbed state,
and compares with `jacobian`. For the irreversible `A + B => C` the worst relative difference is
$1.0 \times 10^{-10}$ ($1.5 \times 10^{-10}$ on a second machine at the same pin). The fixed-temperature derivatives alone have the wrong sign for one entry, and are 0 for
another whose feedback value is $1.4 \times 10^{7}$, so the check does test @eq-ch06-jacobian-feedback. A second card
with the reversible `O + O2 <=> O3` gives $3.5 \times 10^{-10}$ for the forward column. The reverse column is an
expected failure: it is off by a factor of up to $5.9 \times 10^{9}$, because its $\partial k/\partial T$ is the
copied forward one (@sec-ch06-mass-action, Limits).[^ch06-check-g]

<!-- equation-source: eq-ch06-jacobian-feedback reverse-column input differs (D65) -->

### Numerical method

`jacobian` uses the same concentration floor as the rates. It never forms $r_j/c_k$ for an order that is zero, so
trace and zero concentrations do not overflow in the backward pass. Where the condensate of an evaporation column is
zero, $r_j / c_p$ is undefined; the caller then passes the raw rate constants returned by
`forward_with_rate_constants`, and `jacobian` refuses the call without them.

The figure of the Jacobian's sparsity is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |

| declaration | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp KineticsImpl >}} | `KineticsImpl::jacobian` | always |
| Jacobian | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::jacobian >}} | `jacobian` | `evolve_temperature` |
| rate constants | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}} | `forward_with_rate_constants` | always |
| mass-action derivative | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::jacobian >}} | `jacobian` | explicit rate constants at absent reactants |

: Code map of the Jacobian. {#tbl-ch06-jacobian-code}

The mass-action derivative is implemented in `KineticsImpl::jacobian`; there is no separate
`_jacobian_mass_action` helper at this pin. The free functions
declared in {{< code src/kinetics/jacobian_kinetics.hpp >}} (`jacobian_mass_action`, `jacobian_evaporation`) have no
definition at the pin.

### Limits

- At the pin @eq-ch06-jacobian-feedback is generally computed wrongly for the reverse column of a reversible
  reaction: the $\partial k/\partial T$ it uses there is the forward one copied, without $1/K_{c,j}$ and the van 't Hoff
  term of @eq-ch06-mass-action-reverse-dt. This is the recorded defect D65.[^ch06-d65-jac] The check's irreversible
  card passes; its reversible card fails in the reverse column as expected.
- Open question: the drivers of @sec-ch14 pass a volumetric heat capacity at constant pressure as $C_V$; the term
  above is written for constant volume. It matters only with `evolve_temperature` on. Not tested.

[^ch06-d65-jac]: [source: UCzhangxi/kintera#54, row D65 (reverse-reaction `rc_ddT` entries). This text is to be
    updated when that fix merges.]
